subject: Unscheduled maintenance: allocator hotpatch and temporary fallback for Acme.ai
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Lowe <ben.lowe@acme.ai>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 14:12:00 -00:00
Subject: Unscheduled maintenance: allocator hotpatch and temporary fallback for Acme.ai

Hi Avery / Neha / Ben —

Quick update from SRE: we observed a rising rate of short-lived allocator failures tied to a specific request mix that spikes concurrent small-batch allocations (primarily from multi-part embedding + generation calls). The issue can surface as transient 502s or delayed token production when the sequence mix aligns.

We are planning an unscheduled hotpatch to a memory-allocation guard in the serving runtime to close a race that amplifies fragmentation. Planned deployment window: 14:30–15:00 UTC (15–45 minutes; we expect the patch to land in the first 5 minutes and then run a rolling verification).

Customer-facing impact: for the majority of customers this will be transparent. For Acme.ai we expect a brief elevated tail latency for requests that combine large embedding batches with streaming generation — worst-case 20–40s timeouts if they hit the rare allocator path during the rollout. We will:
- Enable model-variant fallback for Acme for the duration of the rollout (route to the previous stable allocator variant)
- Adjust circuit-breaker thresholds for the tenant to avoid client-visible 502s while we verify

Action items for Acme (please):
- Avoid sending batch combos (embedding + stream gen) during 14:25–15:00 UTC if possible
- If you rely on strict sync SLAs, set a higher client timeout for this window (we recommend 60s)

Attachments: allocator_hotpatch.diff (patch summary), customer_impact_matrix_acme.xlsx (per-endpoint risk matrix).

We will post a deploy note in ~20 minutes with a smoke-test summary. Reach me here or on Slack #sre-hotpatch if anything changes.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Lowe <ben.lowe@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 14:19:12 -00:00
Subject: Re: Unscheduled maintenance: allocator hotpatch and temporary fallback for Acme.ai

Thanks for the heads up, Marissa.

Two quick Qs:
1) Will API keys or credentials be rotated for Acme during the change? We cannot accept key rotation without a maintenance window approval.
2) Will we be able to pull request-level traces/logs for any requests that time out so our engineering team can triage?

If fallback to the previous variant is automatic and credentials are unchanged, this should be fine. We'll avoid the multi-part batches in the 14:25–15:00 window.

—Ben
Ben Lowe
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme.ai

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 14:22:45 -00:00
Subject: Re: Unscheduled maintenance: allocator hotpatch and temporary fallback for Acme.ai

On Mon, Jun 7, 2027 at 14:12, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Quick update from SRE: we observed a rising rate of short-lived allocator failures...

Thanks Marissa — tagging in to confirm a couple items for Acme:
- We will NOT rotate API keys. No credential changes.
- Neha: please enable tenant-level fallback routing for Acme before the deploy (route their traffic to the stable allocator variant). That should keep their request failures to a minimum.
- Post-deploy: prepare a short 1–paragraph customer summary and a timestamped list of any Acme-request IDs that experienced >10s latency or 502s; attach that to the HubSpot ticket and share the Drive link.

Marissa: can SRE publish the smoke-check checklist to the shared Drive link (I've attached postdeploy_smoke_checklist.txt to this thread). I'll confirm with Ben once Neha confirms fallback toggled.

Avery Johnson
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Lowe <ben.lowe@acme.ai>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 17:03:05 -00:00
Subject: Re: Unscheduled maintenance: allocator hotpatch and temporary fallback for Acme.ai

Deploy completed at 15:02 UTC; validation finished at 15:18 UTC. Summary:
- Hotpatch applied to running pools (OPS-5492). The allocator guard removes a short-lived race; confirmed fix by reproducing the sample workload and observing no allocator fragmentation on 10 consecutive runs.
- For Acme specifically: we enabled fallback at 14:28 UTC. Acme saw 6 requests with >10s tail latency and 1 transient 502; all affected request IDs are in the attached customer_impact_matrix_acme.xlsx (tab: "events").
- No API keys were rotated. No customer-facing config changes required.

Next steps:
- Formal postmortem (ops+runtime) scheduled for 2027-06-09; we'll include the Acme impact table and remediation timeline.
- We'll follow up with the Acme account packet (short one-paragraph summary + link to the Drive folder and the Jira issue).

Ben — we've shared request-level traces for the affected IDs in the drive link above and added a HubSpot note to DEAL-8732. Let me know if you want a follow-up sync with our runtime team.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
